message: docs(450): state the patch union where the documents still declare the flat shape

edits.find: Status is the part worth reading carefully. `ready` carries usable values. `blocked` and `error` describe a node that still exists and may publish again, and both retain the last known values rather than blanking them. `destroyed` is terminal: the node has been evicted and will never publish again, so drop your local state for it.
edits.replace:
Status is the part worth reading carefully, because it decides what the patch carries rather than labelling something it would carry anyway. `ready` is the only variant that owns a pose: `values`, `sourceProgress` and `sourceRevisions` are three measurements of one successful composition, so a status that did not compose declares none of them. `blocked` and `error` describe a node that still exists and may publish again, and each carries its refusal and nothing else; they are two variants rather than one with a flag, because they are two conditions. `destroyed` is terminal: the node has been evicted and will never publish again, so drop your local state for it.

A non-ready patch used to carry the previous patch's `values`, `sourceProgress` and `sourceRevisions`, so a blocked node republished the last pose and a subscriber reading `patch.values` on it was reading an earlier publication's answer. That is gone, and it is a behaviour change rather than a type refinement. The DOM adapter and `useDomPatch` are unaffected, because both already ignore a non-ready patch and leave the target at the last pose they wrote. A consumer that renders from `values` itself keeps the last `ready` patch it received and renders from that, because the wire does not carry it a second time any more.

The variants have names in the source and are deliberately not on the package entry, so narrow on `status` rather than importing one. `Patch`, `PatchStatus`, `PatchBatch` and `PatchListener` are the exported names, and `PatchStatus` is read off the union rather than spelled beside it, so it cannot name a status that no variant declares.

A patch is frozen, and it is a union discriminated by `status` rather than one shape declaring seven required members at four statuses. Every variant carries `nodeId`, the qualified id, and `revision`, monotonic per node. What it carries beyond those two is exactly what its status owns:

- `ready` owns `values`, deeply frozen; `sourceProgress`, the playhead of the producing node; `sourceRevisions`, the revision of every node that contributed; and `diagnostics`.
- `blocked` and `error` own `diagnostics` and no pose. They are two variants rather than one carrying a flag, because they are two conditions, and a reader that treats them alike writes two arms that return the same thing.
- `destroyed` owns nothing beyond identity and status. A node that will never publish again has nothing to refuse under.

The pose a non-ready patch used to carry forward is the registry's question rather than a member of a patch that is about something else. `PatchRegistry` retains the last accepted `ready` patch per node and answers it through `lastReady(nodeId)`, and unmount, eviction and disposal drop it. That answer is reachable inside the runtime only: `PatchSource` and `ProjectHandle` expose `get` and `subscribeNode`, so forwarding it to a consumer is a public surface change that is owed rather than made. See ADR-098.

edits.find: 8. Publication is deduplicated: unchanged values, progress, source revisions, and status mean no new revision.
edits.replace: 8. Publication is deduplicated per variant: an unchanged status and unchanged inline diagnostics mean no new revision, and for a `ready` patch the values, progress, and source revisions have to be unchanged as well. A variant that owns no pose is never compared on one.

edits.find: - **Patch:** the frozen published value set for one node at one revision.
edits.replace: - **Patch:** the frozen publication for one node at one revision, discriminated by its status: a value set when the node composed, a refusal when it did not, and identity alone once it has been destroyed.

edits.find: - **TR-R-05 Patch shape.** A patch must carry `nodeId`, `revision`, `values`, `sourceProgress`, `sourceRevisions`, `status` of `ready`, `blocked`, or `error`, and `diagnostics`, empty when `ready`. A batch must carry its patches, tick number, seed set, and diagnostics summary.
edits.replace: - **TR-R-05 Patch shape.** A patch must be a union discriminated by `status`, whose four members are `ready`, `blocked`, `error`, and `destroyed`. Every member must carry `nodeId` and `revision`, and must declare only the payload its status owns: `ready` owns `values`, `sourceProgress`, `sourceRevisions`, and `diagnostics`; `blocked` and `error` own `diagnostics`; `destroyed` owns neither. A payload member declared at a status that cannot produce it is a defect rather than a formality, and a reader must narrow on `status` before reading one. `PublishInput` must be discriminated the same way, so no caller can ask for a pose at a status that owns none and no registry decides by hand which members survive a publication. A batch must carry its patches, tick number, seed set, and diagnostics summary. See ADR-098.

edits.find: - **TR-R-08 Deduplication.** Unchanged values, progress, source revisions, status, and inline diagnostics must produce no new revision and no subscriber notification. Implements FR-13.
edits.replace: - **TR-R-08 Deduplication.** Equality is per variant. An unchanged status and unchanged inline diagnostics must produce no new revision and no subscriber notification, and for a `ready` patch the values, progress, and source revisions must be unchanged as well. A variant that owns no pose must not be compared on one. Implements FR-13.

edits.find: Two more readers depend on the product shape. `samePatch` compares all five payload fields unconditionally and is what suppresses a republication, so it decides revision numbers: once a blocked patch stops carrying values, two consecutive blocked patches that differed only in their carried-forward values become equal, the second is suppressed, and the revision sequence a subscriber observes moves. That is observable through `revision` alone. And `#notifyTerminal` builds the terminal patch with `values: {}`, `sourceProgress: 0`, `sourceRevisions: {}` and `diagnostics: []`, every one of which the destroyed variant deletes.
edits.replace: Two more readers depend on the product shape. `samePatch` compares all five payload fields unconditionally and is what suppresses a republication, so it decides revision numbers, and deleting the payload from the non-ready variants shrinks what it compares there to the status and the diagnostics. This record claimed a consequence for the revision sequence and withdraws it. An independent pass established that the scenario as written is unreachable: two consecutive blocked publications that both omit values carry the same previous values by construction, so they were already equal and already suppressed, and if an intervening publication moved the values then they are not consecutive. No concrete case where an observed revision sequence moves has been found, so none is claimed; a guess dressed as a finding is exactly what the guardrails have a record corrected from the run for. And `#notifyTerminal` builds the terminal patch with `values: {}`, `sourceProgress: 0`, `sourceRevisions: {}` and `diagnostics: []`, every one of which the destroyed variant deletes.

edits.find: `PublishInput` is discriminated the same way in the same slice. Eliminating the carry-forward without closing the input just moves the hand-written decision from the registry into every caller of it, which is the second-owner shape the guardrails refuse.
edits.replace: `PublishInput` is discriminated the same way in the same slice. Eliminating the carry-forward without closing the input just moves the hand-written decision from the registry into every caller of it, which is the second-owner shape the guardrails refuse. It mirrors the read side without matching it member for member: two interfaces rather than four, one requiring `values` at `ready` and one covering `blocked` and `error` together, because a reader narrows on `status` to learn what it may read while a caller already knows which refusal it is publishing. That asymmetry buys two refusals at no cost. `destroyed` stops being publishable from outside, so `#notifyTerminal` is the only producer of a terminal patch rather than merely the intended one, and a refusal carries no `sourceProgress`, which the publisher had been passing as a placeholder zero that the carry-forward then overwrote.

That reaches `samePatch`, which becomes an equality per variant rather than one comparison of five fields, and it reaches the React store and the DOM binding, which must narrow to `ready` before reading `values`.
edits.replace: Every read of the union accounts for every variant it can actually receive, and a read that branches ends at the shared `never` sink `domain/exhaustive` already owns, on ADR-092. A reader whose callers cannot hand it every variant satisfies that at its declaration instead of with a predicate: `LivePatch` is the union minus the terminal variant, and typing a parameter with it states once who is allowed to produce a destroyed patch rather than spending a narrowing at each reader that cannot receive one. That reaches `samePatch`, which becomes an equality per variant rather than one comparison of five fields, and it reaches the React store and the DOM binding, which must narrow to `ready` before reading `values`.

edits.find: Revision numbering can move for non-ready patches, for the deduplication reason above. Any case asserting an exact revision after a block is evidence about the old carry-forward and is re-read rather than adjusted to pass.
edits.replace: Revision numbering is not claimed to move, on the withdrawal above. A case asserting an exact revision after a block is still re-read rather than adjusted to pass, because it is evidence about the old carry-forward either way.

edits.find: `PatchBatch.diagnostics` is untouched. Batch diagnostics are the flush's own and are not a patch payload.
edits.replace:
`PatchBatch.diagnostics` is untouched. Batch diagnostics are the flush's own and are not a patch payload.

One behaviour change beyond the deletion, found while converting the source rather than predicted here. A source that has published only `blocked` or `error` and never once `ready` used to answer `{}` through the carry-forward, which `hasValue` reads as published, so its readers composed against an empty input record with no error and no diagnostic. It answers absent now, so `firstPendingEdge` classifies those readers pending and they publish a blocked patch naming the source instead. That is the correct answer rather than a regression: an empty record is not a pose, `graph/references.ts` owns what pending means, and a misconfiguration with no symptom is the thing the guardrails refuse.

The retained pose is reachable inside the runtime only. `lastReady` lives on `PatchRegistry`, and `PatchSource` and `ProjectHandle` expose `get` and `subscribeNode`, so `runtime/publisher-outcome.ts` reads it and no consumer can. `adapters/dom.ts` and `useDomPatch` are unaffected either way, because both ignore a non-ready patch and leave the target at the last pose they wrote. A consumer that renders from `values` itself retains its own last `ready` patch until forwarding the registry's answer onto the consumer surface is decided, and that forwarding is owed rather than done, because it widens a public surface this work does not claim.

edits.find: The work is cut so no slice exceeds the sizing rule in [PR-WORKFLOW.md](./PR-WORKFLOW.md). The first slice decided the retention question with a failing-first case and has landed, which is what makes every later slice mechanical, and the next one owes the complete reader census before any type moves. Then the contract union and `PublishInput`, then `publish`, `samePatch` and `#notifyTerminal` in the registry, then the publisher and the runtime, then the React store and the DOM binding, then the suite. The owning pull request carries the plan, the measured semantic file count, and the exact tested SHA.
edits.replace: The first slice decided the retention question with a failing-first case and landed. The second was the complete reader census, and it corrected this section rather than following it: the four slices planned after it cannot each be green, because deleting a member with no alias stops every unguarded reader compiling in the same `typecheck` run, so the union and all of its readers are one vertical slice with a roughly sixty-file blast radius. The census is the measurement that says so and it lives on the owning pull request rather than being restated here. What is left of the plan is that one slice, and the version bump this record deferred is still owed, against the entry surface the census measured rather than against an unknown one.
